content.title: Linear Stock Rankings Survive Execution in a Thin Market: Forecasting, Selection, and Net Performance on Bursa Malaysia*
content.abstract: For the 300 largest Bursa Malaysia stocks over 2022–2025, we ask whether linear and machine learning forecasts predict return levels, rank stocks, and payoff after trading costs. None predicts the level; only linear models rank stocks. In the predesignated test, a long‐only mean‐variance portfolio built on the OLS ranking earns a net Sharpe ratio of 0.58, not significantly above the FBM KLCI's 0.30. Charging the optimizer for its trades lifts the ratio to 1.16; adjusted for all strategies tested, this portfolio significantly beats a value‐weighted benchmark of the same stocks but only marginal
